action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:

# config-to-document — agent prompts

Prompts for Step 4 of [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md). Fill `<M>` (module), `<m>` (lower case), `<base>` (profile artifact base, absolute), `<bNNN>` / `<tNNN>` (batch), `<lang>` (document language). Every agent saves through `notes.mjs save` from the workspace root (the directory that holds `.sc4sap/`), **no backslash characters** in the text.

**How to save (all prompts):** a whole batch in one heredoc exceeds the Windows command-line limit (`ENAMETOOLONG`). Build the marker text in a file, one or two activities per Bash call — the first call `cat > <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'`, later calls `cat >> <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'` — then save with `node sc4sap/scripts/config/notes.mjs save --module <M> --batch <batch> --kind <kind> --file <file>`. Use a sub-folder of your scratchpad named after the batch and your role (e.g. `b007-writer/b007.draft.txt`) — other agents share the scratchpad, so never write helper files at its top level. Short texts (a review, a few terms) may still go in one heredoc piped to `save` without `--file`.

## 1. Writer — `Agent(subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-<m>-consultant")`

> You write the consultant notes and the reference material of a configuration document for the SAP <M> module of a real system. Read `<base>/config-docs/<M>/notes/_in/<bNNN>.json`: per IMG activity the IMG path, titles, objects (columns, row counts, customer-changed rows, up to 15 sample rows — customer rows first, codes with their fixed-value text in parentheses), check findings and SAP's IMG documentation (`sapDoc`, English).
>
> For EVERY item write, in <lang> (SAP product terms such as Material Block, MRP Area, Plant stay in English):
> - `## purpose` 1–2 sentences: what the setting controls.
> - `## impact` 2–4 bullets: what THIS system's values mean — quote the sample values; describe patterns when rows are many.
> - `## cautions` 1–3 bullets: risks, dependencies, what to check before a change; include every check finding.
> - `## refs` 1–3 bullets: related T-codes, IMG activities, tables.
> - `## sapdoc` 2–5 sentences: the SAP documentation summarised in <lang> (omit when `sapDoc` is empty).
> - `## cases <decision question>` then 2–3 `### case CASE n — <name>` blocks, each with `flow:` 3–5 short steps separated by `>` (prefix `? ` for a decision, `! ` for the end), `desc:` 2–3 sentences, `when:` when it fits, `this: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `this: no — <evidence>`. The cases are the realistic ways to set this activity up; exactly the cases the sample supports are `yes`.
> - `## mix` one sentence: how companies usually combine the cases.
> - `## compare` a Markdown table: first row `| Aspect | CASE 1 | CASE 2 |`, 3–5 rows (setup effort, operation, risk …).
> - `## checklist` 3–5 bullets: questions to decide the setup.
> - `## criteria` lines `rev:` reversibility, `chain:` linked settings, `pre:` prerequisites, `ind:` industry variance, `risk:` common mistakes, `s4:` S/4HANA / Fiori differences, `auth:` authorisation and organisation, `mig:` migration and interfaces, `rec:` default recommendation — one line each.
> - `## sources` 2–4 bullets `- <title> | <source name> | <URL> | <one-sentence summary>`. Official SAP documentation only: SAP Help Portal (help.sap.com), SAP Notes / KBAs (me.sap.com, launchpad.support.sap.com, userapps.support.sap.com, support.sap.com) and SAP Learning (learning.sap.com) — never SAP Community, blogs or third-party sites (the save refuses them). Find them with WebSearch and open each with WebFetch before citing it; never cite a URL you did not open; when no official page fits, cite fewer.
>
> **Items with `"mode": "system"`** already have their general part (purpose, SAP documentation summary, cases, comparison, checklist, criteria, sources) reviewed in the knowledge base — `kb.purpose` and `kb.cases` show it. For them write ONLY `## impact`, `## cautions` (include check findings) and `## verdicts` with one line per KB case: `CASE n: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `CASE n: no — <evidence>`. No web research for these items.
>
> Reading the data: a **customer row** only means its key was recorded in a customer transport (changed, copied or merely saved) — not that the customer created it; a key that follows SAP's naming (no Z/Y/9 prefix, part of a standard series) is a standard entry. Read `C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project/.sc4sap/work/HKT-DEV/config-docs/MM/notes/_in/b028.json`: per IMG activity the IMG path, titles, objects (columns, row counts, customer-changed rows, up to 15 sample rows — customer rows first, codes with their fixed-value text in parentheses), check findings and SAP's IMG documentation (`sapDoc`, English).

For EVERY item write, in Korean (SAP product terms such as Material Block, MRP Area, Plant stay in English):
- `## purpose` 1–2 sentences: what the setting controls.
- `## impact` 2–4 bullets: what THIS system's values mean — quote the sample values; describe patterns when rows are many.
- `## cautions` 1–3 bullets: risks, dependencies, what to check before a change; include every check finding.
- `## refs` 1–3 bullets: related T-codes, IMG activities, tables.
- `## sapdoc` 2–5 sentences: the SAP documentation summarised in Korean (omit when `sapDoc` is empty).
- `## cases <decision question>` then 2–3 `### case CASE n — <name>` blocks, each with `flow:` 3–5 short steps separated by `>` (prefix `? ` for a decision, `! ` for the end), `desc:` 2–3 sentences, `when:` when it fits, `this: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `this: no — <evidence>`. The cases are the realistic ways to set this activity up; exactly the cases the sample supports are `yes`.
- `## mix` one sentence: how companies usually combine the cases.
- `## compare` a Markdown table: first row `| Aspect | CASE 1 | CASE 2 |`, 3–5 rows (setup effort, operation, risk …).
- `## checklist` 3–5 bullets: questions to decide the setup.
- `## criteria` lines `rev:` reversibility, `chain:` linked settings, `pre:` prerequisites, `ind:` industry variance, `risk:` common mistakes, `s4:` S/4HANA / Fiori differences, `auth:` authorisation and organisation, `mig:` migration and interfaces, `rec:` default recommendation — one line each.
- `## sources` 2–4 bullets `- <title> | <source name> | <URL> | <one-sentence summary>`. Official SAP documentation only: SAP Help Portal (help.sap.com), SAP Notes / KBAs (me.sap.com, launchpad.support.sap.com, userapps.support.sap.com, support.sap.com) and SAP Learning (learning.sap.com) — never SAP Community, blogs or third-party sites (the save refuses them). Find them with WebSearch and open each with WebFetch before citing it; never cite a URL you did not open; when no official page fits, cite fewer.

**Items with `"mode": "system"`** already have their general part reviewed in the knowledge base — `kb.purpose` and `kb.cases` show it. For them write ONLY `## impact`, `## cautions` (include check findings) and `## verdicts` with one line per KB case: `CASE n: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `CASE n: no — <evidence>`. No web research for these items.

Reading the data: a **customer row** only means its key was recorded in a customer transport (changed, copied or merely saved) — not that the customer created it; a key that follows SAP's naming (no Z/Y/9 prefix, part of a standard series) is a standard entry. In `snapshot.json`, `_tr` entries that are not `<SID>K` + 6 letters or digits (e.g. `DEVK900133`, `DEVK9A2OEJ`) — SAP command files such as `P30A_C_SFC`, `P30A_C_PI0`, `/SPE/100_CUST`, `SAPK…` — are SAP delivery records, not customer transports. A sample holds at most 15 rows, customer rows first: a row missing from it, or a table showing exactly 1000 rows (the read cap), is never proof that something does not exist. When the sample cannot settle a point, look it up in the full table in `C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project/.sc4sap/work/HKT-DEV/config-docs/MM/snapshot.json` (`tables.<NAME>.rows`) with a small `node -e` filter — never print the whole file — and say "unverified" only when the snapshot cannot settle it either. Be exact with T-codes (verify each one you name).

Hard rules: every statement about this system rests on the given data; never invent values, plants or company facts; SAP Note numbers only when the opened page shows them; one or two sentences per bullet.

Build the marker text in a file, one or two activities per Bash call — the first call `cat > <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'`, later calls `cat >> <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'` — in a scratchpad sub-folder `b028-writer/` (never at the scratchpad top level; no backslash characters in the text). Then from the workspace root `C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project` run `node sc4sap/scripts/config/notes.mjs save --module MM --batch b028 --kind draft --file <file>`: per item `@@ <activity id>` followed by the sections. Fix and re-save until it prints `"ok":true`. Final message: the printed JSON line, plus any activity whose sample did not let you judge this system.

content.text:
## 1) 재시작 이유: Windows 업데이트 자동 재시작

직접 설정한 게 없어도 Windows가 업데이트를 마무리하려고 스스로 재시작했습니다. 이벤트 로그 기록은 다음과 같습니다.

- **2026-10-15 01:52~01:53**: `TrustedInstaller.exe`(Windows 업데이트 설치 서비스)가 SYSTEM 계정으로 재시작을 실행했습니다. 사유는 "운영 체제: 업그레이드(계획됨)"입니다. 업데이트를 마무리하느라 01:50~01:54 사이에 **세 번 연달아** 재시작했습니다.
- 설치된 업데이트: 2026-10 보안 업데이트 KB5127648, .NET Framework 보안 업데이트 KB5127690, 01:46에 받은 Lenovo System Driver Update 26.8.0.29.
- 사용 시간이 **07시~22시**로 설정돼 있습니다. Windows는 이 시간에는 재시작하지 않지만, 그 밖의 시간(새벽 1시대)은 언제든 자동으로 재시작할 수 있습니다. 작업이 밤새 돌고 있었는데 그 시간에 재시작된 것입니다.

다시 막으려면 **설정 → Windows 업데이트 → 고급 옵션**에서 사용 시간을 넓히거나, 긴 작업을 돌리기 전에 **업데이트 일시 중지**(1주)를 켜 두세요.

## 2) 작업 이어서 진행: 시작했습니다

저장된 파일로 확인한 상태입니다.

| 상태 | 배치 |
|---|---|
| 확정 | b001~b025 |
| 초안만 있음, 검토 필요 | b026, b027 |
| 시작 전 | b028~b031 |

재시작 직전 b028과 b030은 작성 중이었는데, 저장 전에 끊겨 결과가 없습니다. 그래서 처음부터 다시 씁니다.

지금 배경에서 6개가 같이 돌고 있습니다.
- **검토 중:** b026, b027
- **작성 중:** b028, b029, b030, b031

앞서 고친 판정 규칙도 이번 지시에 넣었습니다. SAP 납품 기록(`P30A_C_PI0`, `/SPE/100_CUST` 등)은 고객 TR로 세지 않고, 트랜잭션 코드는 하나씩 확인하게 했습니다. 순서는 전과 같습니다. 검토가 끝나 고칠 항목이 나오면 수정본을 받고, 그다음 확정합니다. 배치마다 끝나는 대로 알려드리겠습니다. 배치 하나에 약 40분, 75만 토큰 정도 듭니다.

content.text:
"jev 라이브러리"가 무엇인지 저는 모르겠습니다. `Documents\Projects`에서도 찾아봤는데 아직 아무것도 안 나왔습니다(검색은 계속 돌고 있습니다). 정체를 모르는 상태로 적용 여부를 판단하면 추측이 됩니다. **링크나 패키지 이름(npm/GitHub)을 알려주시면** 이 스킬에 맞는지 확인해 보겠습니다.

"퀄리티는 유지하면서 시간과 토큰을 줄이는 방법"은 지금 구조만 봐도 답할 수 있습니다. 비용은 대부분 웹 조회에서 나오는 것으로 보입니다. 그것도 같은 페이지를 여러 번 엽니다.

## 비용이 새는 곳
배치 하나(12개 활동)는 다음 순서로 진행됩니다.
1. **작성자**가 활동마다 출처 2~4개를 WebSearch로 찾고 WebFetch로 엽니다(배치당 수십 번).
2. **검토자**가 모든 URL을 처음부터 다시 엽니다(같은 횟수만큼 또).
3. **수정본**을 쓸 때 웹 조사를 또 합니다.

즉 같은 help.sap.com 페이지를 2~3번 받아 읽습니다. 지금 `notes.mjs`에는 시스템이 달라도 재사용되는 KB(`~/.sc4sap/kb/config/`)는 있지만, **URL 단위 캐시는 없습니다**.

## 제안 (효과 큰 순)

| # | 방법 | 효과 | 퀄리티 영향 |
|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | **기계적 검증을 스크립트로**: 고객 TR 건수(SAP 납품 기록 제외)를 미리 계산해 입력에 넣고, 언급된 T-code가 실제 있는지 스냅샷의 TSTC로 확인합니다. | 수정 라운드 축소 | 향상. b022, b023 수정 사유 대부분이 이 유형 |

| 4 | **IMG 문서 우선**: 입력에 이미 있는 `sapDoc`을 1차 근거로 삼고, 웹 출처는 활동당 2개 이하로 줄입니다. | 작성 시간 감소 | 출처 수만 줄어듦 |

지금 b026~b031은 기존 방식대로 돌고 있으니 그대로 끝내겠습니다. 스크립트를 중간에 바꾸면 진행 중인 에이전트가 깨질 수 있습니다. 개선은 **이 배치들이 끝난 뒤** 적용해 다음 모듈(SD 등)이나 `--redo`부터 쓰는 게 안전합니다.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

input.prompt: What is jev? Describe exactly what it does, its API/interface (CLI, library, language), how it is installed and used, licensing, supported platforms, and any claims about token/time savings for LLM agents (web browsing, crawling, fetching). Include concrete examples and numbers quoted from the page.

Describe exactly what it does, its API/interface (CLI, library, language), how it is installed and used, licensing, supported platforms, and any claims about token/time savings for LLM agents (web browsing, crawling, fetching). Include concrete examples and numbers quoted from the page.

content.content:
**Jev** is TypeSafe AI's first **System One Model**, a model "built to make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly." It takes unstructured state as input and returns typed probabilistic decisions. It gives up free-form text generation in exchange for speed and structured output. It is in early access.

**Interface:** The page doesn't name a CLI, library, or programming language. It links to docs (docs.typesafe.ai), an API console (console.typesafe.ai), and a playground for early-access users. Output structure is "defined in advance," and the model "never makes type errors," according to the page.

**Installation and usage:** Not described. Access is through early access, with users being brought off a waitlist.

**Licensing:** Not stated for Jev. The page links to a GitHub repo, `system-one-adapter-python`, but describes it as a wrapper that constrains LLMs to output structured decisions. It doesn't say Jev is open source.

**Supported platforms:** Not stated. The page mentions that evals were run "from our laptops on the West Coast," which describes test conditions, not supported platforms.

**Token and time savings for browsing, crawling, or fetching:** The page makes no such claim. The closest content is the Wikiracing demo, where the model picks among "hundreds to thousands of links" while traversing Wikipedia. The page says Jev tended to finish in fewer steps than the LLMs, and that its speedups there were smaller than in other demos.

**Numbers from the page:**
- End-to-end response time: 70ms–500ms, versus 3–329 seconds for frontier LLMs.
- Speedup: 40x–200x for System One-shaped queries; 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper in the workflow evals.
- Input cost: $0.042 per million tokens. Output tokens are listed as free.
- Doom demo: 10 queries per second, costing about $7/hour.
- Maximum choice cardinality: 255.

**Caveats:** The page says the workflow speedups are "on the higher end of real world gains," and that the reference answers, drawn from OpenAI and Anthropic models, likely underestimate the performance of other models. The Wikiracing comparisons used non-reasoning LLM modes.

# SuperClaude for SAP (sc4sap) — Development Rules

This file is the **index** of development rules — NOT a payload to preload. Detailed rules live in `common/` and `exceptions/`. Consult files on demand per [`common/context-loading-protocol.md`](common/context-loading-protocol.md) — 4-tier model: **Tier 1** global mandatory safety baseline (always loaded by every agent: `data-extraction-policy`, `sap-version-reference`, `naming-conventions`; `context-loading-protocol` + `model-routing-rule` are orchestrator-only, read by skills), **Tier 2** role-mandatory per agent group, **Tier 3** triggered reads, **Tier 4** per-task kit. Everything referenced below is MANDATORY for every sc4sap session (agents, skills, direct user requests, pipelines).

## Development Standards — References

| Topic | Reference |
|---|---|
| Naming conventions (Z/Y prefixes, module prefix, includes, FGs, tables, DEs, DOs) | [`common/naming-conventions.md`](common/naming-conventions.md) |
| Field typing priority (Standard DE → CBO DE → new CBO DE → Data Type+Length; never `LIFNR CHAR 10`) | [`common/field-typing-rule.md`](common/field-typing-rule.md) |
| Function Module source convention (inline IMPORTING/EXPORTING/TABLES in FUNCTION statement; no placeholder, no shadow locals) | [`common/function-module-rule.md`](common/function-module-rule.md) |
| SAP version awareness (ECC vs S/4HANA — tables, TCodes, BAPIs, patterns) | [`common/sap-version-reference.md`](common/sap-version-reference.md) |
| ABAP release awareness (syntax availability per release, never emit newer features than `ABAP_RELEASE`) | [`common/abap-release-reference.md`](common/abap-release-reference.md) |
| Clean ABAP coding standards (paradigm-split) | shared baseline [`common/clean-code.md`](common/clean-code.md) + one of [`common/clean-code-oop.md`](common/clean-code-oop.md) or [`common/clean-code-procedural.md`](common/clean-code-procedural.md) chosen from the Phase 1B Paradigm dimension; also pulls in `constant-rule.md`, `text-element-rule.md`, `abap-release-reference.md` |
| Procedural FORM naming (screen-bound suffix) | [`common/procedural-form-naming.md`](common/procedural-form-naming.md) |
| OOP two-class split pattern | [`common/oop-pattern.md`](common/oop-pattern.md) |
| Include structure (Main + conditional includes) | [`common/include-structure.md`](common/include-structure.md) |
| ALV display rules | [`common/alv-rules.md`](common/alv-rules.md) |
| Tabstrip screens (STRIP_CTRL + subscreen area + tab PUSH rows, `CALL SUBSCREEN` in PBO and PAI) | [`common/screen-tabstrip.md`](common/screen-tabstrip.md) |
| OK_CODE binding pattern (one TOP variable + screen NAME + PAI dispatch; never `CASE sy-ucomm`) | [`common/ok-code-pattern.md`](common/ok-code-pattern.md) |
| SPRO lookup protocol (consultant agents, IMG/Customizing) | [`common/spro-lookup.md`](common/spro-lookup.md) |
| Customization lookup protocol (existing Z*/Y* BAdI impl, CMOD, form-exits, appends — mandatory before recommending new enhancements/extensions) | [`common/customization-lookup.md`](common/customization-lookup.md) |
| Data extraction policy (blocklist rule, `acknowledge_risk` hard rule, refusal template) | [`common/data-extraction-policy.md`](common/data-extraction-policy.md) |
| Transport client rule (every `CreateTransport` must receive explicit `client` from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT — never an implicit default) | [`common/transport-client-rule.md`](common/transport-client-rule.md) |
| Blocklist (per-category table lists) | [`exceptions/table_exception.md`](exceptions/table_exception.md) (index) + `exceptions/*.md` section files |

content.content:
If the command fails with `TABLE_READ: table … is not allowed` on an IMG table (`TNODEIMG`, `CUS_IMGACH`), the system's `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` predates the customizing allow rule: stop and tell the user to update it from `abap/zmcp_adt_dispatch_ecc.abap` (setup Step 9) — never work around the dispatcher.

**Step 3 — Extract.** Run in the background (`run_in_background: true`):
```
node scripts/config/extract-config.mjs --module <M> [--areas "<Area 1>,<Area 2>"] [--lang <lang>]
```
It prints progress (`tables n/N`) on stderr and one JSON line at the end: `{ ok, file, counts }`. An interrupted run resumes from its read cache; `--fresh` starts over (use it when the user asks for a refresh of an earlier document). Report the counts when it finishes.

**Step 4 — Consultant notes and reference material (written, then reviewed).** Per IMG activity the notes card (purpose, effect of *this system's* values, cautions, references) and the reference panel (SAP documentation summarised in the document language, 2–3 setup cases with flow diagrams and which one this system follows, comparison table, decision checklist, decision criteria, official SAP sources — Help Portal, Notes / KBAs, Learning — opened and cited) are written by the module consultant agent and reviewed by `sap-critic`; never by the main thread. Prompts: [`notes-prompts.md`](notes-prompts.md) — use them verbatim with the placeholders filled.
0. **Terms first.** `node scripts/config/notes.mjs terms --module <M>` → `terms/_in/tNNN.json` (names SAP has no document-language text for: IMG folders, activity titles, field labels; 150 per batch; translated terms are reused by later runs). Per batch: writer then reviewer, prompt § 4. Skip when it reports 0 terms.
1. **Scope — ask on every run.** `node scripts/config/notes.mjs scopes --module <M>` prints activities and batches per scope (activities with reviewed notes from earlier runs are left out). Ask with one `AskUserQuestion`, each option labelled with its numbers from that output and the cost (one batch ≈ 12 activities, a writer, a reviewer and usually a revision run with web research — measured on MM: about 750k tokens and 40 minutes per batch):
   - `custom` — activities customer transports changed (Recommended)
   - `values` — also standard and empty ones (every activity with a table)
   - `all` — every activity, including transaction-only ones
   - `none` — no notes this run; the document is built without new notes
   Then `node scripts/config/notes.mjs batches --module <M> --scope <scope> --size 12` → `notes/_in/bNNN.json` (numbered after existing batches; `--redo` rewrites reviewed activities too, only when the user asks).
2. **Write** — per batch, `Agent(subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-<m>-consultant")` with prompt § 1 (saves `--kind draft`). Batches run in parallel, at most 4 at a time.
3. **Review** — per batch, `Agent(subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-critic")` with prompt § 2 (saves `--kind review`, prints the `fix` list). The reviewer opens every cited URL.

1	# config-to-document — agent prompts
2	
3	Prompts for Step 4 of [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md). Fill `<M>` (module), `<m>` (lower case), `<base>` (profile artifact base, absolute), `<bNNN>` / `<tNNN>` (batch), `<lang>` (document language). Every agent saves through `notes.mjs save` from the workspace root (the directory that holds `.sc4sap/`), **no backslash characters** in the text.
4	
5	**How to save (all prompts):** a whole batch in one heredoc exceeds the Windows command-line limit (`ENAMETOOLONG`). Build the marker text in a file, one or two activities per Bash call — the first call `cat > <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'`, later calls `cat >> <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'` — then save with `node sc4sap/scripts/config/notes.mjs save --module <M> --batch <batch> --kind <kind> --file <file>`. Use a sub-folder of your scratchpad named after the batch and your role (e.g. `b007-writer/b007.draft.txt`) — other agents share the scratchpad, so never write helper files at its top level. Short texts (a review, a few terms) may still go in one heredoc piped to `save` without `--file`.
6	
7	## 1. Writer — `Agent(subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-<m>-consultant")`
8	
9	> You write the consultant notes and the reference material of a configuration document for the SAP <M> module of a real system. Read `<base>/config-docs/<M>/notes/_in/<bNNN>.json`: per IMG activity the IMG path, titles, objects (columns, row counts, customer-changed rows, up to 15 sample rows — customer rows first, codes with their fixed-value text in parentheses), check findings and SAP's IMG documentation (`sapDoc`, English).
10	>
11	> For EVERY item write, in <lang> (SAP product terms such as Material Block, MRP Area, Plant stay in English):
12	> - `## purpose` 1–2 sentences: what the setting controls.
13	> - `## impact` 2–4 bullets: what THIS system's values mean — quote the sample values; describe patterns when rows are many.
14	> - `## cautions` 1–3 bullets: risks, dependencies, what to check before a change; include every check finding.
15	> - `## refs` 1–3 bullets: related T-codes, IMG activities, tables.
16	> - `## sapdoc` 2–5 sentences: the SAP documentation summarised in <lang> (omit when `sapDoc` is empty).
17	> - `## cases <decision question>` then 2–3 `### case CASE n — <name>` blocks, each with `flow:` 3–5 short steps separated by `>` (prefix `? ` for a decision, `! ` for the end), `desc:` 2–3 sentences, `when:` when it fits, `this: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `this: no — <evidence>`. The cases are the realistic ways to set this activity up; exactly the cases the sample supports are `yes`.
18	> - `## mix` one sentence: how companies usually combine the cases.
19	> - `## compare` a Markdown table: first row `| Aspect | CASE 1 | CASE 2 |`, 3–5 rows (setup effort, operation, risk …).
20	> - `## checklist` 3–5 bullets: questions to decide the setup.
21	> - `## criteria` lines `rev:` reversibility, `chain:` linked settings, `pre:` prerequisites, `ind:` industry variance, `risk:` common mistakes, `s4:` S/4HANA / Fiori differences, `auth:` authorisation and organisation, `mig:` migration and interfaces, `rec:` default recommendation — one line each.
22	> - `## sources` 2–4 bullets `- <title> | <source name> | <URL> | <one-sentence summary>`. Official SAP documentation only: SAP Help Portal (help.sap.com), SAP Notes / KBAs (me.sap.com, launchpad.support.sap.com, userapps.support.sap.com, support.sap.com) and SAP Learning (learning.sap.com) — never SAP Community, blogs or third-party sites (the save refuses them). Find them with WebSearch and open each with WebFetch before citing it; never cite a URL you did not open; when no official page fits, cite fewer.
23	>
24	> **Items with `"mode": "system"`** already have their general part (purpose, SAP documentation summary, cases, comparison, checklist, criteria, sources) reviewed in the knowledge base — `kb.purpose` and `kb.cases` show it. For them write ONLY `## impact`, `## cautions` (include check findings) and `## verdicts` with one line per KB case: `CASE n: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `CASE n: no — <evidence>`. No web research for these items.

# config-to-document — agent prompts

Prompts for Step 4 of [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md). Fill `<M>` (module), `<m>` (lower case), `<base>` (profile artifact base, absolute), `<bNNN>` / `<tNNN>` (batch), `<lang>` (document language). Every agent saves through `notes.mjs save` from the workspace root (the directory that holds `.sc4sap/`), **no backslash characters** in the text.

**How to save (all prompts):** a whole batch in one heredoc exceeds the Windows command-line limit (`ENAMETOOLONG`). Build the marker text in a file, one or two activities per Bash call — the first call `cat > <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'`, later calls `cat >> <file> <<'NOTES_EOF'` — then save with `node sc4sap/scripts/config/notes.mjs save --module <M> --batch <batch> --kind <kind> --file <file>`. Use a sub-folder of your scratchpad named after the batch and your role (e.g. `b007-writer/b007.draft.txt`) — other agents share the scratchpad, so never write helper files at its top level. Short texts (a review, a few terms) may still go in one heredoc piped to `save` without `--file`.

>
> For EVERY item write, in <lang> (SAP product terms such as Material Block, MRP Area, Plant stay in English):
> - `## purpose` 1–2 sentences: what the setting controls.
> - `## impact` 2–4 bullets: what THIS system's values mean — quote the sample values; describe patterns when rows are many.
> - `## cautions` 1–3 bullets: risks, dependencies, what to check before a change; include every check finding.
> - `## refs` 1–3 bullets: related T-codes, IMG activities, tables.
> - `## sapdoc` 2–5 sentences: the SAP documentation summarised in <lang> (omit when `sapDoc` is empty).
> - `## cases <decision question>` then 2–3 `### case CASE n — <name>` blocks, each with `flow:` 3–5 short steps separated by `>` (prefix `? ` for a decision, `! ` for the end), `desc:` 2–3 sentences, `when:` when it fits, `this: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `this: no — <evidence>`. The cases are the realistic ways to set this activity up; exactly the cases the sample supports are `yes`.
> - `## mix` one sentence: how companies usually combine the cases.
> - `## compare` a Markdown table: first row `| Aspect | CASE 1 | CASE 2 |`, 3–5 rows (setup effort, operation, risk …).
> - `## checklist` 3–5 bullets: questions to decide the setup.
> - `## criteria` lines `rev:` reversibility, `chain:` linked settings, `pre:` prerequisites, `ind:` industry variance, `risk:` common mistakes, `s4:` S/4HANA / Fiori differences, `auth:` authorisation and organisation, `mig:` migration and interfaces, `rec:` default recommendation — one line each.
> - `## sources` 2–4 bullets `- <title> | <source name> | <URL> | <one-sentence summary>`. Official SAP documentation only: SAP Help Portal (help.sap.com), SAP Notes / KBAs (me.sap.com, launchpad.support.sap.com, userapps.support.sap.com, support.sap.com) and SAP Learning (learning.sap.com) — never SAP Community, blogs or third-party sites (the save refuses them). Find them with WebSearch and open each with WebFetch before citing it; never cite a URL you did not open; when no official page fits, cite fewer.
>

For them write ONLY `## impact`, `## cautions` (include check findings) and `## verdicts` with one line per KB case: `CASE n: yes — <evidence from the sample>` or `CASE n: no — <evidence>`. No web research for these items.

When the sample cannot settle a point, look it up in the full table in `<base>/config-docs/<M>/snapshot.json` (`tables.<NAME>.rows`) with a small `node -e` filter — never print the whole file — and say "unverified" only when the snapshot cannot settle it either.
>
> Hard rules: every statement about this system rests on the given data; never invent values, plants or company facts; SAP Note numbers only when the opened page shows them; one or two sentences per bullet.
>

## 2. Reviewer — `Agent(subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-critic")`

Read the input `<base>/config-docs/<M>/notes/_in/<bNNN>.json` and the notes `<base>/config-docs/<M>/notes/<bNNN>.draft.json`. Save: `node sc4sap/scripts/config/notes.mjs save --module <M> --batch <tNNN> --kind draft <<'NOTES_EOF'` with one line per term `<id> = <translation>`, every id present. Final message: the printed JSON line.

Reviewer (`sc4sap:sap-critic` with `model: "sonnet"` — a term check needs no Opus):
> Check the translations in `<base>/config-docs/<M>/terms/<tNNN>.draft.json` against the English in `…/terms/_in/<tNNN>.json`: wrong SAP meaning, a product term translated that SAP keeps in English, inconsistent naming of the same thing. Save only the corrections: `node sc4sap/scripts/config/notes.mjs save --module <M> --batch <tNNN> --kind review <<'NOTES_EOF'` with lines `<id> = <corrected> | <reason>` (an empty heredoc when all are fine). Final message: the printed JSON line and the number of corrections.

지금까지 진행 상황입니다.

## 배치 진행
- **확정:** b001~b027. b026은 3개, b027은 6개 활동 수정본이 반영됐습니다.
- **수정 중:** b031. 6개 중 2개를 고칩니다. 회사 코드를 T001과 대조하고, 9999일 규칙에 "4.70 문서 기준, 이 릴리스에서는 미확인"이라는 단서를 붙이는 내용입니다.
- **새 방식으로 검토 중:** b028, b029, b030. 지금은 Haiku 사전 검사 단계이고, 끝나면 Opus 검토로 넘어갑니다.

## 1~3번 구현 내용
1. **출처 캐시**(`notes-sources.mjs`): 검토를 통과한 활동의 출처를 `~/.sc4sap/kb/config/MM/sources-ko.json`에 쌓습니다. 기존 배치에서 **검증된 URL 248개**로 채웠습니다. 다음 배치 입력에는 `knownSources`가 붙습니다. 작성자는 요약을 그대로 가져다 쓰고 웹을 다시 열지 않으며, 검토자는 `new`/`changed` 출처만 엽니다. 남은 배치 입력으로 시험해 보니 항목의 약 절반에 안내가 붙었습니다.
2. **기계 검사**(`notes-lint.mjs`, 0.5초, 토큰 0):
   - 언급된 T-code가 실제로 있는지, 어떤 프로그램이고 어떤 SM30 뷰를 여는지 확인합니다. 결과는 시스템별 캐시에 37개가 쌓였습니다. 예: OMRX는 V_169L, OBA7은 V_T003을 엽니다.
   - "고객 운송 N행" 같은 문장은 스냅샷 테이블에서 고객 TR만으로 다시 센 값과 비교합니다.
   - 점검 결과가 본문에서 빠졌는지 확인합니다.
   - 사후 확인: b022 초안에 돌렸더니, 실제 검토에서 지적된 **T156(392→195)**과 **T158(14→9)**을 잡아냈습니다. 오탐도 몇 건 있지만 표시만 하는 용도입니다.
3. **검토 분리**: 기계 검사 → Haiku(`sap-checker`)가 샘플과 대조 → Opus(`sap-critic`)가 SAP 의미만 판단하는 순서입니다. `notes-prompts.md`와 SKILL.md(110줄)에 반영했습니다.

이번 b028~b030 검토가 끝나면, 기존 방식의 검토(배치당 약 12만~17만 토큰)와 Opus 토큰 사용량을 비교해서 알려드리겠습니다. 앞서 말씀드린 대로 출처 재사용 효과는 이번 시험에 포함되지 않습니다.

## Jev는 맞지 않습니다
페이지를 확인한 결과, Jev는 크롤러나 문서 처리 라이브러리가 아닙니다. 정해진 선택지(최대 255개) 중 하나를 70~500ms 안에 고르는 **분류 전용 모델 API**입니다. 이 스킬에 맞지 않는 이유는 세 가지입니다.
- 비용이 큰 작업은 한국어 노트 작성, 공식 문서 열람, SAP 의미 판단입니다. 셋 다 생성이나 추론이 필요해서 Jev가 할 수 없습니다.
- 선택지형 판단(T-code 존재, 고객 행 수 등)은 이번에 스크립트로 처리해서, 모델 자체가 필요 없어졌습니다.
- 아직 얼리 액세스인 외부 API에 고객 시스템의 설정값을 보내야 합니다.

content.text:
짧게 답하면 **적용할 수 있는 곳은 있지만 이득은 작고, 지금 도입할 만한 곳은 없습니다.** 이유는 아래와 같습니다.

## Jev가 잘하는 일
한 번에 하나씩, 정해진 선택지(최대 255개) 중 하나를 빠르게 고르는 일입니다. 근거 문장을 쓰거나, 코드를 인용하거나, 여러 단계로 추론하는 일은 하지 못합니다.

## sc4sap 스킬별 검토

| 스킬 / 부분 | 선택지형 판단? | 판단 |
|---|---|---|
| `ask-consultant` 모듈 라우팅 (질문 → SD/MM/FI… 15개 중 하나) | 예, 딱 맞는 모양 | **이득 거의 없음.** 지금은 메인 스레드가 키워드 규칙으로 같은 턴 안에서 정하므로(`SKILL.md:63-75`) 추가 비용이 0에 가깝습니다. |
| `package-to-process` 프로세스 묶기 (프로그램 → PR/PO/GR/IR 단계) | 일부 | **후보.** 객체가 많을 때 분류만 Jev에 맡길 수 있습니다. 다만 코드 의미를 이해해야 하는 판단이라 품질이 검증되지 않았고, 묶은 뒤 쓰는 서술은 어차피 LLM이 해야 합니다. |
| `analyze-cbo-obj` / `sap-stocker` 객체 용도 분류 | 일부 | 같은 이유로 후보입니다. 다만 Haiku로 이미 싸게 처리하고 있습니다. |
| `analyze-code` Haiku 탐지기 (규칙별 위반 여부) | 예/아니오 판단 | **맞지 않음.** 다음 단계의 근거 확인에 해당 코드 줄 인용이 필요한데, Jev는 선택값만 돌려줍니다. |
| `analyze-symptom`, `create-program`, `program-to-spec`/`manual` | 아님 | 비용 대부분이 추론과 생성입니다. |
| PreToolUse 훅 (blocklist, permission-approver) | 예 | **넣으면 안 됨.** 보안 관문은 확률 모델이 아니라 규칙으로 판정해야 합니다. |

## 공통 걸림돌
1. **데이터 반출:** 고객 ABAP 소스, 설정값, 객체 목록을 아직 얼리 액세스인 외부 API로 보내야 합니다. sc4sap의 데이터 추출 정책과 정면으로 부딪히고, 고객사 승인도 필요합니다.
2. **비용 구조가 안 맞음:** 이번에 config-to-document에서 확인했듯 토큰 대부분은 생성, 웹 열람, 의미 판단에서 나갑니다. 선택지형 판단은 대부분 이미 스크립트, 키워드 규칙, Haiku로 처리하고 있어서 Jev가 줄일 몫이 작습니다.
3. **의존성:** Claude/Agent SDK 스택에 외부 API 키와 장애 지점이 하나 더 생깁니다.

## 굳이 시험해 본다면
`package-to-process`의 분류 단계를 고르겠습니다. 객체 수십~수백 개를 같은 정답 세트로 두고 Haiku와 Jev의 정확도, 속도, 비용을 비교하는 방식입니다. 그래도 데이터 반출 문제를 먼저 풀어야 해서 지금 당장은 권하지 않습니다.

그 사이 b028~b030은 Haiku 사전 검사를 진행 중입니다. 끝나는 대로 Opus 검토를 이어가겠습니다.

content.text:
Jev 질문에는 위에서 답했습니다. 다른 스킬에도 쓸 수는 있지만 이득은 작고, 지금 도입할 곳은 없다는 결론입니다.

새 방식 시험 상황입니다.
- **b029:** Haiku 사전 검사를 거쳐 Opus 검토를 시작했습니다.
  - Haiku는 34줄을 냈는데, 대부분 "샘플에 없음"이라는 잡음이었습니다. 작성자가 스냅샷 전체를 근거로 쓴 것이라 오류가 아닙니다. 그래서 프롬프트를 고쳐 실제로 값이 어긋나는 것만 보고하게 했습니다.
  - OBYC 지적 3건은 기계 검사 스크립트가 OBYC를 엉뚱한 IMG 활동 제목에 연결해서 생긴 오탐이었습니다. 이 연결 규칙은 고쳤습니다.
- **b028, b030:** Haiku 검사가 아직 돌고 있습니다.
- 사전 검사 비용은 Haiku 약 13만 토큰(1.8분)이었습니다. 금액 기준으로는 Opus의 일부 수준입니다. 실제로 이득인지는 Opus 검토 토큰이 기존(배치당 12만~17만)보다 줄었는지 보고 판단하겠습니다.

Haiku 사전 검사 3개가 모두 끝났고, 지금은 b028, b029, b030의 Opus 검토 3개가 돌고 있습니다.

**Haiku 검사에서 얻은 것**
- 실제로 쓸 만한 단서가 배치마다 5~7개 나왔습니다.
  - b028: 입력에 BWTKZ 열이 있는데도 "BWTKZ 필드가 없다"고 쓴 곳
  - b030: 객체 이름 오기(VVC_T682_MR → VV_T682_MR), 다른 활동의 IMG 경로를 적은 곳, 잘린 테이블에서 센 고객 행 수
- 나머지 대부분(배치당 30~80줄)은 "15행 샘플에 없음"이라는 잡음이었습니다. 이 배치들은 프롬프트를 고치기 전에 돌렸기 때문입니다. Opus에게는 메인 스레드가 추린 목록만 넘겼습니다.
- Haiku 비용은 배치당 약 13만~17만 토큰, 2~3분이었습니다.

**기계 검사 수정**
Haiku 결과 덕분에 기계 검사 오류 세 가지를 찾아 고쳤습니다.
- IMG 활동이 객체로만 들고 있는 T-code를, 그 T-code의 용도인 것처럼 연결하던 문제를 고쳤습니다(OBYC가 리베이트 활동 제목에 붙던 경우).
- "41행(customer 37행)"처럼 괄호로 고객 수를 따로 적은 문장을 오탐하던 문제를 고쳤습니다.
- 잘린 테이블에서 센 수는 항상 확인 대상으로 표시합니다.

고친 뒤에도 b022 사후 확인에서 실제 지적(T156, T158)은 그대로 잡힙니다.

Opus 검토 3개가 끝나면, 기존 검토와 토큰·소요 시간·지적 품질을 비교해서 정리하겠습니다. 기존 검토는 배치당 12만~17만 토큰, 5~7분이었습니다.

b029 검토 결과로 첫 비교 수치가 나왔습니다. 솔직히 말씀드리면, **이번 시험에서는 Opus 토큰이 줄지 않았습니다.**

| | Opus 검토 | 추가 비용 |
|---|---|---|
| 기존 방식 b026 / b027 | 17.3만 / 17.2만 토큰, 6.6~7.2분 | — |
| 새 방식 b029 | 16.3만 토큰, 6.6분, 도구 43회 | Haiku 12.7만 + 기계 검사 0 |

이유는 두 가지입니다.
1. **출처 19개를 전부 새로 열었습니다.** b029 입력이 캐시보다 먼저 만들어져서 작성자가 검증된 출처를 재사용하지 못했고, 그래서 전부 `new`였습니다. 1번(출처 캐시)의 효과는 이번 시험에 아예 들어가지 않았습니다.
2. **Haiku 단서는 Opus가 다시 확인해야 합니다.** b029에서 넘긴 7개 중 실제 문제는 0개였고 7개 모두 오탐이었습니다. Opus가 찾은 진짜 문제 2개(WKA_004 의미 모순, WKA_006 출처 요약)는 Haiku 목록에 없었습니다. 즉 Haiku 단계가 Opus 작업을 줄이지 못하고, 확인할 거리만 늘렸습니다.

현재 판단은 이렇습니다.
- **1번(출처 캐시)**: 유지합니다. 효과는 다음 실행부터 나옵니다. b029 검토 후 캐시는 264개로 늘었습니다.
- **2번(기계 검사)**: 유지합니다. 토큰이 0이고 실제 오류(T156, 잘린 테이블 수)를 잡습니다.
- **3번(Haiku 단계)**: b028, b030 결과까지 보고 판단하겠습니다. 거기서도 비슷하면 **Haiku 단계는 빼고**, 기계 검사 결과만 Opus에게 넘기는 쪽을 권하겠습니다.

진행: b029는 수정 중(2개)이고, b028과 b030은 Opus 검토 중입니다.

content.text:
Haiku 단계를 뺐습니다.

- **`notes-prompts.md`:** 기존 2b(Haiku 검사)를 지우고, 검토는 기계 검사 다음 바로 Opus로 넘어가는 두 단계로 바꿨습니다. Opus 지시도 고쳤습니다. 기계 검사가 `ok: false`로 표시한 수와 잘린 테이블의 수를 단서로 확인하고, T-code가 노트에서 쓰인 용도와 맞는지 보게 했습니다. 왜 뺐는지는 한 줄로 적어 두었습니다. 같은 실험을 반복하지 않게 하려는 것입니다.
- **SKILL.md:** 3단계 설명을 같은 내용으로 고쳤습니다. 줄 수는 SKILL.md 110줄, 프롬프트 53줄로 둘 다 200줄 아래입니다.

빼기로 한 근거는 이번 세 배치의 결과입니다.

| 배치 | Opus 토큰 / 도구 호출 | Haiku 토큰 | Haiku 단서 → 실제 문제 |
|---|---|---|---|
| b029 | 16.3만 / 43 | 12.7만 | 7 → 0 |
| b028 | 15.4만 / 59 | 16.1만 | 5 → 2 |
| b030 | 19.5만 / 60 | 17.0만 | 7 → 4 |
| 기존 방식 b026 / b027 | 17.3만 / 17.2만 | — | — |

- Opus 비용은 줄지 않았습니다.
- b030의 "실제 문제" 4개 중 2개는 잘린 테이블에서 센 수였는데, 이건 **기계 검사가 이미 잡은 것**입니다.
- 나머지 단서는 대부분 Opus가 아니라고 확인하느라 시간만 들었습니다.

남은 것은 1번과 2번입니다.
- **출처 캐시:** 검증된 URL 264개가 쌓여 있습니다. 다음 실행(SD 등 다른 모듈, 또는 `--redo`)부터 작성자와 검토자가 웹 조회를 건너뜁니다.
- **기계 검사:** 토큰 0, 0.5초로 고객 행 수 오류, 잘린 테이블의 수, T-code 실존을 잡습니다.

배치 진행 상황입니다.
- **확정:** b001~b027, b029, b031
- **수정 중:** b028(6개), b030(8개). 끝나면 MM 노트 배치가 전부 끝나고, 다음 단계(KB 승격, 문서 빌드)로 넘어갈 수 있습니다.

커밋은 하지 않았습니다. 새 파일은 `scripts/config/notes-lint.mjs`와 `notes-sources.mjs`이고, 수정한 파일은 `notes.mjs`와 스킬 MD 2개입니다. `git status`에 같이 보이는 `build-config-doc.mjs`, `extract-config.mjs`, 테스트 파일 등의 변경은 이번 세션 전부터 커밋되지 않은 채 있던 것입니다.
